text: How the gate accepts a TLAPS proof (#360). A project selects ratified invariants by name in its manifest's tlaps field; selecting one claims evidence and changes no statement, so it isn't in the lock. The proof of an invariant Inv lives at .invariant/proofs/Inv.tla as the body of a module the gate writes, which extends the ratified model and TLAPS; the proof may extend only TLAPS's standard modules besides. It defines the inductive invariant IndInv_Inv and proves three lemmas whose statements the gate fixes: Init implies it, it and a Next step or stutter imply it after the step, and it implies Inv. The gate appends the only temporal theorem, Spec implies always Inv, proved by PTL, which LS4 decides. A proof may not add an axiom, assumption, constant, variable, instance or module, omit a proof, cite TLAPS's own temporal rules, or use ENABLED, the cdot operator, temporal operators, CASE expressions or exponents, which tlapm's open soundness issues touch (tlaplus/tlapm 309, 304 and 324). The model must have the gate's spec and none of those constructs, assumptions or unproved theorems, and may extend only standard modules. tlapm runs offline in a throwaway copy in strict mode, preferring its standard library and using no fingerprints from earlier runs, and a proof counts only when tlapm exits cleanly with every obligation proved or trivial. The evidence binds the SHA-256 of the model and of the proof, since Init and Next aren't pinned, names the library facts the proof cites, which those modules only state, and records tlapm's commit and its backends' versions. The fingerprint leaves out which backend proved each obligation, which timing decides.
